description: verification-architecture.md's R6 proof-table row (line 37) was only PARTIALLY corrected by iteration-2's FIND-006 fix. FIND-006 explicitly enumerated five locations carrying the stale '180-char result cap' ground-truth claim and fixed all five, including the LAST clause of this same R6 table row ('assert ledger.jsonl's own result field... is still <=900 chars (corrected, iteration 2, resolves FIND-006...)'). But an EARLIER clause in the exact same table cell was never touched: 'simulate one skill_error wake (mock skill exits 1 with >180-char stdout)->one line with slot,layer:'tool_logic',exit_code,detail LONGER than 180 chars'. This is not a ground-truth factual claim (so FIND-006's five-location enumeration correctly did not list it), but it IS a live test-fixture threshold, and it is now stale relative to the corrected 900/4000 numbers everywhere else in this same requirement. R6's entire stated rationale (Problem section, lines 14-19: 'even 900 characters is not enough to see where in a multi-step fallback chain a skill actually broke') is that harness-failures.jsonl's 4000-char detail field must retain diagnostic content BEYOND what the ledger's own (now-900-char, post-task-#119) result field can show. A test fixture of '>180-char stdout' does not exercise this at all: any mock stdout between 181 and 900 characters satisfies '>180-char stdout' AND 'detail LONGER than 180 chars' trivially, while ALSO fitting entirely within the existing 900-char result cap -- meaning this test would pass identically whether or not R6's new 4000-char detail capture actually preserves anything beyond what the pre-existing ledger.jsonl already showed. Worse, if Phase 2a authors this literally (e.g. a 250-char mock stdout), the test would also pass under an INCORRECT implementation that caps detail at, say, 500 or 900 chars instead of the required 4000 -- as long as the mock fixture stays under that wrong cap. The test as literally worded therefore cannot distinguish a correct 4000-char detail implementation from several classes of incorrect (too-small-cap) implementations, and does not verify the requirement's actual value proposition. Fix: replace '>180-char stdout' / 'LONGER than 180 chars' with a fixture that exceeds the CURRENT result cap, e.g. '>900-char stdout (e.g. 2000 chars)' and assert 'detail retains content beyond the point where the corresponding ledger.jsonl result field for the same wake was truncated at 900 chars, up to detail's own 4000-char cap' -- this is the only test shape that actually proves R6's stated diagnostic-preservation claim.

evidence.snippet: simulate one `skill_error` wake (mock skill exits 1 with >180-char stdout)->one line with `slot`,`layer:'tool_logic'`,`exit_code`,`detail` LONGER than 180 chars
